vo: This cancer cell has nine minutes to live.
A patient's own T cell, rebuilt in a lab with a brand-new receptor.
It hunts one marker on cancer cells: CD19.
In about three minutes, it locks on.
Then it fires toxic granules, straight into the cancer cell.
And it's already moving on, to the next one.
